lead.hed: U.S. and British forces sank the retired frigate Klakring in the North Atlantic
lead.insight: U.S. 6th Fleet said Wednesday that Exercise Atlantic Thunder ended Sept. 25 with the sinking of the decommissioned guided-missile frigate ex-USS Klakring. USS Paul Ignatius fired an anti-surface Standard Missile-6. USS Massachusetts, a newly commissioned Virginia-class submarine, finished the ship with a Mk 48 torpedo. The Royal Navy fired its Naval Strike Missile and Sea Venom. U.S. Air Force F-15Es and P-8 patrol planes also took part. The frigate entered service in 1983 and left it in 2013. Official still is a KC-135 crew at RAF Mildenhall on Sept. 21, before a tanker mission in the same exercise, not the sinking itself.
lead.image_credit: Senior Airman Aidan Martínez Rosiere · DVIDS 9970026 · Public domain · Airmen of the 100th Air Refueling Wing pose with a KC-135 at RAF Mildenhall, England, before an Atlantic Thunder tanker mission, Sept. 21, 2026.

political.hed: The Army picked five companies to prototype a longer-range strike missile
political.insight: Redstone Arsenal said the Army signed five Other Transaction Authority agreements on Sept. 29 for Precision Strike Missile Increment 4 prototypes. The companies are Anduril, Castelion, Lockheed Martin, Mach Industries, and RTX. Each missile must launch from a HIMARS truck and hit moving ships or land targets at 1,000 kilometers or more. The Army plans a competitive fly-off in fiscal 2027 and a final fly-off in fiscal 2028. A prototype race, not a production buy. Defense News reported the same release Wednesday.

political.hed: HII won a $5.1 billion overhaul of the carrier Harry S. Truman
political.insight: HII said Tuesday that Newport News Shipbuilding received a $5,099,973,132 contract to refuel and overhaul USS Harry S. Truman. Options, if taken, raise the total to $5,183,380,744. The yard will refuel the reactors and modernize propulsion and combat systems. The work is meant to carry the ship through the second half of its service life. Defense News reported the award Wednesday. A contract notice, not a sailing date.

tech.hed: An essay says Fulton Sheen belongs with the friends of political freedom
tech.insight: Law & Liberty, Wednesday: the essay marks the Catholic Church’s beatification of Archbishop Fulton J. Sheen on Sept. 24, the last step before canonization. The writer says Sheen’s radio and television work, including the 1950s program Life Is Worth Living, made hard ideas accessible, and that readers who are not Catholic should still weigh what he argued for political freedom. Essay, not a Vatican decree and not a vote.

culture.hed: First Things marks fifty years of the Hyde Amendment
culture.insight: First Things, Wednesday: in 1976, freshman Rep. Henry Hyde of Illinois attached one sentence to a health appropriations bill barring those funds from paying for abortions except where the mother’s life was in danger. The magazine says that rider became law fifty years ago today and calls it the most consequential legislation in the pro-life movement. An anniversary essay, not a new floor vote.
